newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds slip as punt teeters at parity vs stg.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds slip as punt teeters at parity vs stg.

text.p: Irish government bonds slipped in patchy trade on Thursday as EMU confidence was dented by the Irish pound's slide against sterling, dealers said.

"U.S. data has taken a backseat after the UK rate rise on Wednesday which has concentrated our attention on the currency market. Breaking parity with sterling seems certain now and we hope it doesn't damage EMU convergence trading," a dealer said.
By 1611 GMT, the eight percent bond due 2000 was 18 pence weaker at 106.12 to yield 6.12 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 was down 10p at 107.35 to yield 6.82.
The eight percent bond due 2015 was at 110.65.
"The central bank seems to be buying up Irish pounds to stall further depreciation against sterling, and there has been a noticeable nervousness in the market today," one dealer said.
The Irish pound slid further against sterling on Thursday, and was perched at parity by 1645 GMT, down from 1.0031 at Wednesday's close.
UK gilts also slipped into negative territory on Thursday as fears over pensions costs under a single European currency hit the market.

Dealers said U.S.jobs data on Friday remained the immediate focus of the market. Economists polled by Reuters forecast a 212,000 payrolls increase for October while the Purchasing Managers Index is expected to make a downward adjustment to 53.0.
Dealers said Irish live register unemployment figures on Friday are expected to drop by about 10,000 for October, reflecting jobs growth and reduced social welfare fraud.
